ui.hubMetaTitle: Where to Stay in Korea: Best Areas in Seoul, Busan & Jeju
ui.hubMetaDesc: Where to stay in Korea — the best neighborhoods in Seoul, Busan and Jeju for first-timers, nightlife, beaches, culture and budget, with hotel links.
ui.hubTagline: Pick the right area in each city — by vibe, not just price.
ui.cityTagline: The best areas & neighborhoods — chosen by vibe, not just price.
ui.typesIntro: Not sure what to book? Here's how Korea's main lodging types compare — and who each one suits.

seoul.name: Seoul
seoul.metaTitle: Where to Stay in Seoul: Best Areas & Neighborhoods (2026)
seoul.intro: Seoul is huge, but the subway makes any neighborhood workable — so choose by the vibe you want. First-timers do best somewhere central like Myeongdong or Insadong; night owls love Hongdae; and Gangnam is the modern, upscale side of the river.

areas.name: Myeongdong
areas.vibe: The classic first-time base — central, packed with hotels, street food and beauty shops, and walkable to Gyeongbokgung and N Seoul Tower.
areas.near: Airport bus stops here; Lines 4 & 2. Can be busy and touristy.

areas.name: Hongdae
areas.vibe: Young, artsy university district with live buskers, indie shops, cafes and the city's best nightlife. Great value guesthouses and hostels.
areas.near: AREX runs direct to Incheon Airport (~50 min). Lines 2 & 6.

areas.name: Gangnam
areas.vibe: Sleek, business-y and pricey — luxury hotels, COEX mall, K-pop spots around Apgujeong. Further from the historic centre.
areas.near: Lines 2, 3, 7 & Sinbundang; convenient for Suseo/SRT trains.

areas.name: Insadong & Jongno
areas.vibe: Traditional heart of Seoul — tea houses, galleries, hanok stays and a short walk to Gyeongbokgung, Bukchon and Changdeokgung. Quieter at night.
areas.near: Lines 1, 3 & 5. Very walkable for sightseeing.

areas.name: Itaewon
areas.vibe: Seoul's most international quarter — global restaurants, the most halal options in the city, and a lively bar scene.
areas.near: Line 6; close to Yongsan and N Seoul Tower.

areas.name: Dongdaemun
areas.vibe: Around-the-clock fashion malls, the futuristic DDP and cheap late-night eats. Handy if you want to shop till dawn.
areas.near: Lines 1, 2 & 4; central and well-connected.

seoul.budget: On a budget? Hongdae and Myeongdong are packed with dorms, guesthouses and hostels — great value and social, and popular with younger travellers.
notes: Seoul rewards a central base — anywhere along Subway Line 2 puts most sights within a short ride, and 24-hour convenience stores and late trains mean you rarely feel stranded.

Rates run highest around Myeongdong and Gangnam, while Hongdae, Mapo and Jongno give better value with plenty of character. Many hotels hold your bags before check-in, which helps after an early KTX or airport arrival.

busan.name: Busan
busan.metaTitle: Where to Stay in Busan: Best Areas & Beaches (2026)
busan.intro: Busan is a beach city, so most visitors base themselves near the sea. Haeundae is the resort favourite; Gwangalli has the best night view; Seomyeon is the central transport-and-food hub; and Nampo-dong is the old-town market side.

areas.name: Haeundae
areas.vibe: Busan's most famous beach — high-rise resort hotels, the aquarium, Blueline Park sky capsule and a lively seafront.
areas.near: Line 2. A bit removed from the old town, but the beach makes up for it.

areas.name: Gwangalli
areas.vibe: Relaxed beach with a front-row view of the Gwangan Bridge light show, plus a young cafe-and-bar strip. Great for sunset.
areas.near: Line 2 (Gwangan); a short hop from Haeundae.

areas.name: Seomyeon
areas.vibe: Busan's downtown crossroads — shopping, endless restaurants and nightlife, and the easiest transfers across the city.
areas.near: Lines 1 & 2 interchange; the most central base.

areas.name: Nampo-dong & Jagalchi
areas.vibe: Historic Busan — Jagalchi fish market, Gukje market, BIFF Square street food and Gamcheon Culture Village nearby. Good value.
areas.near: Line 1; walkable, atmospheric, budget-friendly.

areas.name: Songjeong
areas.vibe: A calmer beach just east of Haeundae popular with surfers, with guesthouses, surf hostels and sea-view stays.
areas.near: Blueline Park coastal rail and Haeundae are a short ride away.

areas.name: Busan Station & Choryang
areas.vibe: Around the KTX station — well-priced hotels, the port and Choryang's hillside alleys, handy for arrivals and Nampo-dong.
areas.near: KTX and Line 1; an easy first or last night in the city.

busan.budget: On a budget? Nampo-dong, Seomyeon and the areas near the beaches have plenty of guesthouses and hostels.
notes: Busan stretches along the coast, so choose your base by mood: Haeundae for the beach and resort hotels, Seomyeon for shopping and the best transit links, or Nampo-dong for markets and old-town streets.
The metro connects them all, though rush-hour roads are slow. Sea-view rooms in Haeundae sell out early for the summer months, so book well ahead if you come in July or August.

jeju.name: Jeju
jeju.metaTitle: Where to Stay in Jeju: North vs South (2026)
jeju.intro: Jeju splits into a north side (Jeju City — where you land) and a south side (Seogwipo — warmer, greener, closer to the famous nature). You'll want a rental car either way; pick the side nearest the sights you care about.

areas.name: Jeju City (north)
areas.vibe: Where the airport, Dongmun night market and most buses are — the practical, well-serviced base with the widest hotel choice.
areas.near: Jeju International Airport; best for short trips and nightlife.

areas.name: Seogwipo (south)
areas.vibe: Warmer, lush southern hub near Cheonjiyeon Waterfall, Jusangjeolli cliffs and Seongsan Ilchulbong — closer to Jeju's postcard scenery.
areas.near: ~1 hr from the airport by car; scenic and calmer.

areas.name: Jungmun
areas.vibe: Jeju's resort belt — big-name beach resorts, golf and the Jungmun Saekdal beach, ideal for a relaxed stay-put holiday.
areas.near: Near Seogwipo, south coast; resort-focused.

areas.name: Aewol (west coast)
areas.vibe: A scenic west-coast stretch of café-restaurants and stylish pensions along the shore, a relaxed base away from the city.
areas.near: A car is recommended; a short drive west of Jeju City.

areas.name: Seongsan (east)
areas.vibe: Beside Seongsan Ilchulbong on the east coast — pensions and guesthouses handy for the sunrise hike, the Udo ferry and Seopjikoji.
areas.near: Great for touring east Jeju; a car is recommended.

jeju.budget: On a budget? Jeju City has guesthouses and hostels near the bus terminal and Dongmun Market — many are social hubs for solo travelers and hikers.
notes: Jeju is a big island best split in two: many visitors spend the first nights near Jeju City in the north, close to the airport, then move to Seogwipo in the south for the waterfalls and Jungmun resort beaches.
A rental car makes far more sense here than public buses, and where you stay along the coast decides whether you wake to sunrise or catch the sunset over the sea.

gyeongju.name: Gyeongju
gyeongju.metaTitle: Where to Stay in Gyeongju: Best Areas (2026)
gyeongju.intro: Gyeongju, Korea’s ancient Silla capital, is compact and spreads across a few bases: the Bomun Lake resort belt for hotels and calm, the old downtown around the royal tombs and the Hwangnidan-gil cafe street for sights on foot, and the area near Bulguksa for an early temple start.

areas.name: Bomun Lake Resort
areas.vibe: A purpose-built resort zone around a lake, with the biggest hotels, spas and easy access to Bulguksa — quiet and green, a short ride from the sights.
areas.near: A short ride to downtown by bus or taxi; best for comfort and families.

areas.name: Downtown & Hwangnidan-gil
areas.vibe: The walkable old centre beside the royal tombs, Cheomseongdae and the trendy Hwangnidan-gil cafe-and-boutique street — most historic sights are on foot.
areas.near: Walk to Daereungwon, Cheomseongdae and Wolji; guesthouses and boutique stays.

areas.name: Near Bulguksa
areas.vibe: The greener eastern side near Bulguksa and Seokguram, good for a peaceful base and an early temple visit before the crowds.
areas.near: Closest to Bulguksa and Seokguram; a bus or taxi ride from downtown.

gyeongju.budget: On a budget? Hwangnidan-gil and the downtown area have hanok guesthouses and hostels within walking distance of the royal tombs and the night-lit Wolji Pond.
notes: Gyeongju is compact and walkable around the historic centre, so staying near Bomun Lake or the old town keeps the royal tombs, Cheomseongdae and the night-lit sights within easy reach.

Traditional hanok guesthouses here are a highlight and often better value than in Seoul. As a day-trip favourite the city fills up on weekends and in cherry-blossom season, so reserve early for spring.

jeonju.name: Jeonju
jeonju.metaTitle: Where to Stay in Jeonju: Best Areas (2026)
jeonju.intro: Jeonju is compact and easy: sleep in a traditional hanok inside the Hanok Village to be steps from the sights and food, or pick a modern hotel around the downtown and station for comfort and transport.

areas.name: Hanok Village & around
areas.vibe: Sleep in a restored hanok guesthouse right among the lanes, tea houses and street food — the most atmospheric base, and walkable to everything.
areas.near: In the heart of the sights; book ahead on weekends.

areas.name: Downtown & Jeonju Station
areas.vibe: Modern hotels around the downtown and station, handy for buses and the KTX — more comfort and choice, a short ride from the hanok village.
areas.near: Best for train/bus connections; quieter at night.

jeonju.budget: On a budget? The Hanok Village and its side streets are full of affordable hanok guesthouses — a night on a traditional ondol floor is part of the experience.
notes: In Jeonju the Hanok Village is the reason most people come, and sleeping in a traditional hanok inside it — heated ondol floors and a small courtyard — is the signature experience, steps from the bibimbap restaurants and street food.
Rooms are simple but atmospheric. If you'd rather have a modern hotel, base near the Jeonju bus terminal or the Gaeksa area and reach the village in a short taxi ride.

gangneung.name: Gangneung
gangneung.metaTitle: Where to Stay in Gangneung: Best Areas (2026)
gangneung.intro: Gangneung splits between the sea and the centre: base at Gyeongpo or Anmok beach for sand, cafes and coffee, or stay downtown near the station for transport and an easy KTX hop from Seoul.

areas.name: Gyeongpo & Anmok Beach
areas.vibe: Right by the East Sea beach, pine-backed lake and the famous Anmok coffee street — the relaxed, scenic base most visitors want.
areas.near: On the beach; a short ride from the station and downtown.

areas.name: Downtown & Gangneung Station
areas.vibe: Around the KTX station and central market, handy for buses down the coast and an easy arrival from Seoul.
areas.near: Best for transport and markets; a short ride to the beaches.

gangneung.budget: On a budget? Near Gyeongpo Beach and the station you'll find guesthouses and pensions, with coffee-street cafés and the sea an easy walk or bus ride away.
notes: Gangneung is all about the coast: stay near Gyeongpo or Anmok Beach for sunrise over the sea and the famous coffee-street cafes, or near Gangneung Station if you're arriving on the fast KTX from Seoul.
Summer weekends and the winter-sea season get busy, so book beachfront rooms ahead. Many travellers pair it with nearby Jeongdongjin for its sunrise train views.

suwon.name: Suwon
suwon.metaTitle: Where to Stay in Suwon: Best Areas (2026)
suwon.intro: Suwon is an easy day trip or overnight from Seoul: stay in the old town by Hwaseong Fortress to walk the walls and Haenggung Palace, or pick a hotel near Suwon Station for transport and shopping.

areas.name: Hwaseong old town
areas.vibe: Inside the fortress walls near Haenggung Palace and the Haenggung-dong cafe lanes — the most characterful base, steps from the main sights.
areas.near: Walk to the walls and palace; guesthouses and small hotels.

areas.name: Suwon Station area
areas.vibe: Around the station with big hotels, department stores and easy trains — practical and well-connected to Seoul.
areas.near: Best for transport and shopping; a short ride to the fortress.

notes: Suwon works well as an easy overnight from Seoul: stay inside the Hwaseong Fortress old town to walk the walls and Haenggung Palace at your own pace, or pick a hotel by Suwon Station for department stores and quick trains.
The old-town guesthouses are quieter and full of character, while the station area is more practical. It's close enough that a day trip also works if you'd rather sleep in Seoul.

incheon.name: Incheon
incheon.metaTitle: Where to Stay in Incheon: Yeongjongdo & Airport (2026)
incheon.intro: Incheon is most travellers’ arrival point — and a growing K-pop concert base. Yeongjong Island, home to Incheon Airport and the Inspire Arena, is where many overseas fans stay for shows and layovers; the planned city of Songdo adds modern hotels, and the old open-port district has Korea’s oldest Chinatown and the seaside at Wolmido.

areas.name: Yeongjong Island (Airport & Inspire Arena)
areas.vibe: The island with Incheon Airport and the Inspire Arena entertainment resort — a favourite base for overseas K-pop concert-goers and anyone with an early or late flight, with airport hotels and a big resort complex.
areas.near: On the AREX line from the airport; a short shuttle or taxi to Inspire Arena.

areas.name: Songdo
areas.vibe: A sleek, planned district of skyscrapers, parks and convention centres like Central Park and Songdo Convensia — modern hotels and a calm, spacious feel.
areas.near: Incheon subway Line 1; linked to the airport by bridge.

areas.name: Open Port & Wolmido
areas.vibe: Incheon’s historic harbour quarter — Korea’s oldest Chinatown, mural streets and the Wolmido seaside boardwalk with its old-school fun fair.
areas.near: Line 1 to Incheon Station; walkable and atmospheric.

incheon.budget: On a budget? Around Unseo Station on Yeongjong Island (one AREX stop from the airport) there are cheaper airport hotels, guesthouses and dorms — handy for an early flight or an Inspire Arena concert.
notes: Incheon is where most trips begin or end, so it's a smart base for early flights: hotels around Incheon Airport and on Yeongjong Island let you sleep minutes from the terminal, some with free shuttles.
For the city itself, stay near the Open Port and Chinatown for atmosphere and easy Line 1 access to Seoul. A last night here beats a pre-dawn dash across the capital.

sokcho.name: Sokcho
sokcho.metaTitle: Where to stay in Sokcho — Seoraksan & beach areas
sokcho.intro: Sokcho is the gateway to Seoraksan National Park and a laid-back East Sea beach town. Most visitors base near the beach or the Seoraksan entrance.

areas.name: Sokcho Beach & Harbor
areas.vibe: The main beach and harbor area, close to the fish market, Abai Village and buses toward Seoraksan.
areas.near: Handy for restaurants, ferries and the express bus terminal.

areas.name: Seorak-dong (Seoraksan entrance)
areas.vibe: Right by the Seoraksan National Park gate and cable car, with pensions and resort hotels among the mountains.
areas.near: Best if hiking is your priority; quieter after dark.

areas.name: Downtown & Bus Terminal
areas.vibe: Central Sokcho near the terminals, with cheaper hotels and motels and easy links to the beach and Seoraksan.
areas.near: Convenient for arriving, leaving and day trips.

sokcho.budget: On a budget? Sokcho has guesthouses and hostels near the beach and Jungang Market, plus mountain pensions near Seoraksan that split well between friends.
notes: Sokcho is the gateway to Seoraksan, so stay near the Expo Tower or the harbour for sea views and the fish market, then reach the national park by a short bus.

Rooms near the beach fill quickly in summer and during the autumn foliage, the peak season for Seoraksan. Buses from Seoul arrive at the Sokcho terminal, a handy area for cheaper motels and onward connections.

daegu.name: Daegu
daegu.metaTitle: Where to Stay in Daegu: Best Areas (2026)
daegu.intro: Daegu is compact and easy: base yourself downtown around Dongseongno for shopping and food, or near Dongdaegu Station for fast KTX trains and a quick hop to Seomun Market.

areas.name: Dongseongno (downtown)
areas.vibe: Daegu's buzzing central shopping district, walkable to markets, cafes and the modern-history alleys.
areas.near: Steps from Seomun Market and Kim Kwang-seok Street; plenty of mid-range hotels.

areas.name: Dongdaegu Station
areas.vibe: Around the main KTX station with big hotels and the bus terminal — the easiest arrival point and a fast base for day trips.
areas.near: Direct KTX to Seoul and Busan; malls and dining next door.

notes: Daegu is compact, so a downtown base around Dongseongno keeps the markets, cafes and modern-history alleys on your doorstep, while a hotel by Dongdaegu Station gives you fast KTX links and the bus terminal for day trips.
The city is famously hot in midsummer, so a room with strong air-conditioning is worth checking. Seomun night market is an easy walk from most central hotels.

gwangju.name: Gwangju
gwangju.metaTitle: Where to Stay in Gwangju: Best Areas (2026)
gwangju.intro: Gwangju is the art-and-food hub of the southwest. Stay downtown near the Asia Culture Center for culture and nightlife, or out in the Sangmu district for newer hotels and easy transit.

areas.name: Downtown (Chungjang-ro)
areas.vibe: The old central shopping street by the Asia Culture Center — cafes, galleries and street food, lively after dark.
areas.near: Walk to the ACC and markets; guesthouses and business hotels.

areas.name: Sangmu district
areas.vibe: A modern planned district with newer hotels, restaurants and a subway line into the centre.
areas.near: Handy for business travellers; a short ride to downtown.

notes: In Gwangju the downtown Chungjang-ro area keeps you close to the Asia Culture Center, street food and nightlife, while the newer Sangmu district has modern hotels and a subway line into the centre.
It's a relaxed city with shorter queues than Seoul or Busan, so mid-range hotels are good value. Base downtown if you want to walk to dinner and culture in the evenings.

andong.name: Andong
andong.metaTitle: Where to Stay in Andong: Best Areas (2026)
andong.intro: Andong is the heart of Korean Confucian heritage. Stay in a traditional hanok at Hahoe Village for the full experience, or near Andong Station and downtown for restaurants and easy buses to the sights.

areas.name: Hahoe Village
areas.vibe: Sleep in a centuries-old tiled or thatched house inside the UNESCO folk village — quiet, atmospheric and utterly local.
areas.near: Book a hanok homestay; the mask museum and river are on the doorstep.

areas.name: Downtown & Andong Station
areas.vibe: The compact town centre with the old market, Andong jjimdak restaurants and buses out to Hahoe and the seowon.
areas.near: Best for dining and transport; ordinary hotels and motels.

notes: Andong is spread out, so decide between atmosphere and convenience: a traditional hanok homestay in or near Hahoe Folk Village is unforgettable but quiet and rural, while the downtown and Andong Station area keeps you near restaurants, the old market and buses to the sights.
Book the hanok stays ahead, as there are only a handful. Andong jjimdak is a must-eat, and the central hotels sit closest to it.

yeosu.name: Yeosu
yeosu.metaTitle: Where to Stay in Yeosu: Best Areas (2026)
yeosu.intro: Yeosu is best enjoyed by the water: base yourself around the Expo waterfront for sea-view hotels and the cable car, or across the Dolsan Bridge for the famous night sea and fresh seafood.

areas.name: Yeosu Expo & Waterfront
areas.vibe: Modern hotels and resorts around the old Expo site and Ungcheon, steps from the marine cable car and the lit-up night-sea promenade.
areas.near: Best for sea views and the cable car; walkable waterfront.

areas.name: Dolsan Island
areas.vibe: Over the rainbow-lit Dolsan Bridge — pensions and guesthouses with the classic Yeosu night-sea view and streets of fresh seafood.
areas.near: Great for sunsets and a Hyangiram day trip; a bridge from downtown.

yeosu.budget: A sea-view room by the Expo waterfront costs more than a Dolsan pension, but both put the night sea on your doorstep.
notes: Yeosu is all about the night sea, so a room with a water view — around the Expo waterfront or across on Dolsan Island — is worth it, with the Dolsan Bridge and cable car lighting up after dark.
Summer weekends and festival dates fill fast, so book ahead. The KTX runs to Yeosu-Expo Station, a handy base right by the waterfront.

tongyeong.name: Tongyeong
tongyeong.metaTitle: Where to Stay in Tongyeong: Best Areas (2026)
tongyeong.intro: Tongyeong is a harbour town of islands and murals: stay near Gangguan Port to walk to Dongpirang and the market, or over by the cable car for quieter sea-and-island views.

areas.name: Gangguan Port & downtown
areas.vibe: Around the Gangguan waterfront and Jungang Market — walkable to the Dongpirang mural village, the ferry piers and the famous honey-bread stalls.
areas.near: Best for food and sightseeing on foot; island ferries leave nearby.

areas.name: Mireuksan & cable car side
areas.vibe: Near the Tongyeong cable car and the Hallyeo-waterway lookouts — quieter hotels and resorts with sweeping sea-and-island views.
areas.near: Good for the cable car and coastal drives; a short ride to the port.

tongyeong.budget: Downtown guesthouses near Gangguan are cheap and central, while resort rooms near Mireuksan cost more for the views.
notes: Tongyeong rewards staying near Gangguan Port — you can walk to Dongpirang, Jungang Market and the ferry terminal, and eat your way through honey bread and fresh seafood.
It's the hopping-off point for the Hallyeo islands such as Hansando, so check ferry times and book harbour-side rooms early in summer.

types.name: Hotels
types.desc: From business hotels to five-star resorts, with a front desk, breakfast and daily cleaning. The easiest choice if you value convenience and English-speaking staff.
types.tip: Compare rates and cancellation terms on Agoda or the hotel's own site.

types.name: Guesthouses & hostels
types.desc: Dorm beds and small private rooms, often run by friendly hosts, with common areas that make them social. Popular with solo and young travelers.
types.tip: Great value near Hongdae, Myeongdong and beach towns; female-only dorms are usually available.

types.name: Hanok stays
types.desc: Sleep in a restored traditional Korean house with wooden beams, paper doors and a warm ondol floor. Concentrated in Jeonju, Bukchon in Seoul and Gyeongju.
types.tip: Rooms can be simple and floor-based — ask whether the bathroom is private.

types.name: Pensions
types.desc: Self-contained holiday houses or cabins, often with a kitchen and a barbecue, common on Jeju and in mountain and beach areas. Best split between friends or family.
types.tip: You usually need a car; check whether cooking gear and towels are provided.

types.name: Templestay
types.desc: Spend a night at a Buddhist temple with meditation, tea and temple meals — a calm cultural experience rather than a hotel.
types.tip: Book through the official Templestay program; early mornings are part of the experience.

types.name: Jjimjilbang (sauna)
types.desc: Korean bath-houses with sauna rooms and a shared sleeping hall. Not a hotel, but a cheap, safe option for a short night or a late arrival.
types.tip: You sleep on the floor in a communal room, so bring earplugs; bathing areas are separated by gender.

types.name: Serviced apartments & officetels
types.desc: Apartment-style rooms with a kitchen and laundry, handy for longer visits or families who prefer to self-cater. Common in Seoul and Busan.
types.tip: Check the minimum stay — some are rented by the week or month.
